description: The PATIENTS table contains demographic and mortality information for patients in the database. It includes unique patient identifiers (SUBJECT_ID), gender, date of birth (DOB), dates of death from various sources (DOD, DOD_HOSP, DOD_SSN), and an expiration flag (EXPIRE_FLAG) indicating patient mortality status. Each row is uniquely identified by ROW_ID.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: The unique identifier for each patient.

columns.name: GENDER
columns.description: The gender of the patient, recorded as 'M' (male) or 'F' (female).

columns.name: DOB
columns.description: The date of birth of the patient.

columns.name: DOD
columns.description: Date of death for the patient.

columns.name: DOD_HOSP
columns.description: Date of death as recorded by the hospital.

columns.name: DOD_SSN
columns.description: Date of death as recorded by the Social Security Administration.

columns.name: EXPIRE_FLAG
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the patient has expired (1) or not (0).

description: The `SERVICES` table tracks patient transfers between different hospital services or departments. Each row represents a single patient transfer, identified by a unique `ROW_ID`. The table includes the patient's identifier (`SUBJECT_ID`), hospital admission identifier (`HADM_ID`), the date and time of the transfer (`TRANSFERTIME`), the previous service the patient was on (`PREV_SERVICE`), and the current service the patient is on (`CURR_SERVICE`). This table can be used to analyze patient flow within the hospital.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: The patient identifier, unique to a patient across the entire database.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: The hospital admission identifier, unique to a patient's hospital stay.

columns.name: TRANSFERTIME
columns.description: The date and time when a patient was transferred to a new service or location.

columns.name: PREV_SERVICE
columns.description: The service the patient was on prior to the current transfer, represented by a department code.

columns.name: CURR_SERVICE
columns.description: The service the patient is currently on, represented by a department code.

description: The TRANSFERS table contains information about patient movement within the hospital, specifically admissions, transfers, and discharges between different care units and wards. It includes timestamps for arrival and departure, the length of stay in each location, and identifiers for the patient, hospital admission, and ICU stay. The table also specifies the source database for the data.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for a patient.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for a patient's hospital admission.

columns.name: ICUSTAY_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for a patient's stay in the ICU.

columns.name: DBSOURCE
columns.description: Source database for the data, indicating whether the data originated from 'carevue', 'metavision', or 'both'.

columns.name: EVENTTYPE
columns.description: Type of event related to patient movement, such as 'admit', 'transfer', or 'discharge'.

columns.name: PREV_CAREUNIT
columns.description: The patient's previous care unit, e.g., 'NWARD', 'SICU'.

columns.name: CURR_CAREUNIT
columns.description: The patient's current care unit, e.g., 'NWARD', 'MICU'.

columns.name: PREV_WARDID
columns.description: Identifier for the ward the patient was previously in.

columns.name: CURR_WARDID
columns.description: Identifier for the ward the patient is currently in.

columns.name: INTIME
columns.description: Timestamp indicating when the patient was admitted/transferred into the current location (ICU or ward).

columns.name: OUTTIME
columns.description: Timestamp indicating when the patient was discharged/transferred out of the current location (ICU or ward).

columns.name: LOS
columns.description: Length of stay, in days, in the current location (ICU or ward).

description: The ADMISSIONS table contains information about each hospital admission for patients in the database. It includes patient demographics, admission and discharge timestamps, admission types and locations, insurance details, diagnoses, and flags indicating in-hospital mortality and the presence of chart event data. This table serves as a key source for analyzing patient journeys within the hospital system.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the dataset.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each patient.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each hospital admission.

columns.name: ADMITTIME
columns.description: Date and time of hospital admission.

columns.name: DISCHTIME
columns.description: Date and time of hospital discharge.

columns.name: DEATHTIME
columns.description: Date and time of death for patients who expired in the hospital. Null if the patient did not die during the hospital admission.

columns.name: ADMISSION_TYPE
columns.description: Type of hospital admission (e.g., EMERGENCY, ELECTIVE, NEWBORN).

columns.name: ADMISSION_LOCATION
columns.description: Location of the patient prior to admission to the hospital.

columns.name: DISCHARGE_LOCATION
columns.description: Location to which the patient was discharged (e.g., home, skilled nursing facility, expired).

columns.name: INSURANCE
columns.description: Type of insurance coverage the patient has (e.g. Government, Private, Self Pay).

columns.name: LANGUAGE
columns.description: Primary language spoken by the patient.

columns.name: RELIGION
columns.description: Patient's self-identified religion.

columns.name: MARITAL_STATUS
columns.description: Patient's marital status.

columns.name: ETHNICITY
columns.description: Patient's ethnicity.

columns.name: EDREGTIME
columns.description: Date and time the patient was registered in the emergency department.

columns.name: EDOUTTIME
columns.description: Date and time the patient left the emergency department.

columns.name: DIAGNOSIS
columns.description: Diagnosis for the patient's hospital admission.

columns.name: HOSPITAL_EXPIRE_FLAG
columns.description: Indicates whether the patient expired in the hospital: 1 = expired, 0 = did not expire.

columns.name: HAS_CHARTEVENTS_DATA
columns.description: Indicates whether the patient has data in the CHARTEVENTS table: 1 = has data, 0 = does not have data.

description: The DRGCODES table contains Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) codes assigned to patient hospital admissions. It provides information on the type of DRG coding system used (e.g., APR or MS), the DRG code itself, a description of the code, and severity/mortality risk associated with the DRG. This table links patient admissions (HADM_ID) to specific DRG classifications for billing and diagnostic analysis.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: The patient identifier. Each unique SUBJECT_ID represents a single patient.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: The hospital admission identifier. Each unique HADM_ID represents a single hospital visit for a patient.

columns.name: DRG_TYPE
columns.description: The type of Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) coding system used. Values include 'APR' (All Patient Refined) and 'MS' (Medicare Severity).

columns.name: DRG_CODE
columns.description: The Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) code assigned to the patient's hospital stay. This code is used for billing and classification of diagnoses.

columns.name: DESCRIPTION
columns.description: A textual description of the Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) code. Provides a human-readable explanation of the DRG_CODE.

columns.name: DRG_SEVERITY
columns.description: The severity level associated with the Diagnosis Related Group (DRG). Higher values indicate greater severity of illness.

columns.name: DRG_MORTALITY
columns.description: The mortality risk associated with the Diagnosis Related Group (DRG).  Indicates the likelihood of mortality for patients within this DRG.

description: The ICUSTAYS table contains information on individual ICU stays for patients within the database. It provides unique identifiers for each stay, the associated patient and hospital admission, the source database, the care units and wards involved, admission and discharge timestamps, and the calculated length of stay in the ICU. This table can be used to analyze ICU utilization, patient flow, and length of stay patterns.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the dataset.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each patient.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each hospital admission.

columns.name: ICUSTAY_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each ICU stay.

columns.name: DBSOURCE
columns.description: The database source the data was extracted from; values include 'carevue', 'metavision' or 'both'.

columns.name: FIRST_CAREUNIT
columns.description: The first care unit the patient was admitted to during the ICU stay. Possible values include CCU, CSRU, MICU, NICU, SICU, and TSICU.

columns.name: LAST_CAREUNIT
columns.description: The last care unit the patient was in during the ICU stay. Possible values include CCU, CSRU, MICU, NICU, SICU, and TSICU.

columns.name: FIRST_WARDID
columns.description: The ward ID of the patient at the start of the ICU stay.

columns.name: LAST_WARDID
columns.description: The ward ID of the patient at the end of the ICU stay.

columns.name: INTIME
columns.description: The timestamp of when the patient was admitted to the ICU.

columns.name: OUTTIME
columns.description: The timestamp of when the patient was discharged from the ICU.

columns.name: LOS
columns.description: The length of stay (LOS) in the ICU, calculated as the difference between OUTTIME and INTIME in days.

description: The CAREGIVERS table contains information about caregivers, including a unique identifier (CGID), a descriptive label, and a more detailed description. Each row is uniquely identified by ROW_ID. The table likely serves as a reference table for categorizing and describing different types or aspects of caregivers within a clinical context.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the dataset.

columns.name: CGID
columns.description: Identifier for the caregiver group, referencing a related table (e.g., CARE_GROUP_TABLE).

columns.name: LABEL
columns.description: Category or type assigned to the caregiver, providing a classification for different caregiver roles or specializations.

columns.name: DESCRIPTION
columns.description: A free text field providing a description of the concept or term.
